request: Create a lesson comparing combined item-level sorting accuracy with an equal-bin mean. Require evidence for adding counts and a limited interpretation.
objective: Pool distinct audited items with unequal bin sizes and distinguish description from causes of sorting accuracy.

sources.text: Fictional recycling audit: the lobby bin contained sixteen inspected items, of which four met the sorting rule. The courtyard bin contained thirty-six inspected items, of which twenty-seven met the same rule. Both audits used the same list of acceptable items at the same Friday collection.
Items were individually labeled and belonged to one bin only; none were transferred or counted twice. The audit did not record who used each bin or why an item was placed there.
The requested statistic concerns all52 inspected items. A note instead suggests averaging the two bin percentages with equal weight. No other collection days were inspected.
